subject: plastic shopping bag
title: What If a Plastic Bag Could Send You to Prison? In Kenya It Can

scenes.text: What if carrying a plastic bag could put you in prison for four years? In Kenya, it can.
Before 2017, Kenyan supermarkets handed out about 100 million plastic bags a year. They clogged drains, choked rivers and carpeted roadsides.
Cattle grazed on them. In Nairobi slaughterhouses, vets reported pulling as many as 20 bags from a single cow's stomach.
So on August 28th, 2017, making, selling or carrying one became a crime: up to 4 million shillings, around 40,000 dollars, or four years in jail.
Within two years officials said about 80 percent of people had stopped using them, and streets and rivers were visibly cleaner.
But a bag that costs a cent is hard to kill. Smugglers now sneak them in from neighbouring countries, one truckload at a time.

description:
What if carrying a plastic bag could send you to prison? Since 28 August 2017, Kenya has enforced the world's toughest plastic bag ban: making, selling or using one carries a fine of up to 4 million shillings (around 38,000 to 40,000 US dollars) or up to four years in jail.
Before the ban, Kenyan supermarkets handed out about 100 million bags a year, and animal health officials in Nairobi reported removing up to 20 bags from the stomach of a single slaughtered cow. Two years in, the government said roughly 80 percent of people had stopped using them, though bags are still smuggled in across the borders.
